description:
`apply_bulk_update` opens sessions only for matched issues that actually need a change, matching the session-budget guarantee already tested for automatic transitions.

## Background

`apply_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`) opens a preflight session and a publication session for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes - cost 2*|matched|. The automatic-transitions path already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap in-memory eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session.

Add a pure `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop(&Issue) -> bool` prefilter over the already-listed issues. It is Issue-local and no-op-only: it skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds (state equal, labels present or absent, priority, gate and assignee state), all decidable from the listed `Issue` alone. Potentially invalid updates are not prefiltered - they still open sessions so the same authoritative in-session validation produces the same per-issue error results as before; repository-dependent validity never moves out of the session, and the prefilter only skips, never authorizes.

The session-open bound is C*|matched issues that are not provable no-ops|, where C is the per-mutation session constant (currently 2: preflight plus publication). The budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoding it, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, seeds K matched issues of which K-J already hold their target values, and asserts C*J session opens.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `apply_bulk_update` opens sessions only for matched issues that are not provable no-ops; for K matched issues of which J require a change, session opens equal C*J where C is the per-mutation session constant.
- [hard] REQ-02: `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop` is a pure, Issue-local predicate that skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds; it never authorizes an update and never moves repository-dependent validity out of the session.
- [hard] REQ-03: An issue whose update is potentially invalid still opens a session and yields the same per-issue error result as before the change.
- [hard] REQ-04: The session-budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, and asserts C*J for K seeded issues with K-J already at their target values.

## Notes

The change is behavior-preserving for update results: only the number of sessions opened for provable no-ops changes. Do not hardcode C; a single-issue baseline run yields it. Recording a bulk-mutation scenario in the benchmark harness is separate work.
title: Bulk-update eligibility prefilter and session budget
